summary: This standards-track memo defines an Extensible Provisioning Protocol mapping for managing E.164 telephone numbers stored in a shared registry. It extends the EPP domain name mapping with extra features.

eli5.summary: Phone numbers can be stored and managed in a shared registry like domain names. This document tells registries how to add, change and delete them.

subtitle: How a registry adds, reads and changes phone-number routing records through EPP.

tldr.problem: ENUM uses DNS records to connect E.164 phone numbers to services, but registries needed a standard way to provision those records in a shared central repository.
tldr.mechanism: An XML extension to the EPP domain name mapping adds NAPTR record elements to the create and update commands and to the info response.
tldr.outcome: Registries and clients get one schema for managing the ENUM records of an E.164 domain name, from which DNS data can later be published.

today: RFC 4114 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the EPP domain name mapping of RFC 3731 for use with ENUM as defined in RFC 3761.

sections.title: What the Mapping Does
sections.content:
This document defines an E.164 number mapping for version 1.0 of the Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP). It is an extension of the EPP domain name mapping (RFC 3731), written in XML 1.0 with XML Schema. Readers need to understand the EPP core protocol (RFC 3730) first, because it describes the command and response structures.

ENUM (RFC 3761) describes how DNS can identify the services tied to an E.164 number. This mapping covers the provisioning side: managing E.164 numbers held in a shared central repository. The information exchanged can then be taken from the repository and used to publish the DNS resource records that ENUM describes.
sections.eli5: ENUM is like a phone book entry that says how to reach someone. This document is the form a registry fills in to write those entries.

sections.title: E.164 Domain Names and NAPTR Fields
sections.content:
An E.164 domain name is an E.164 number translated into domain name syntax as ENUM describes. The labels used in that name space are a policy matter outside this document.

ENUM uses NAPTR records to list the ways of contacting a node. Several NAPTR fields are optional under RFC 3403, but RFC 3761 processing rules need some of them, so this document sets field requirements to match RFC 3761. The fields map to XML as follows:

  • Order and Preference: 16-bit unsigned integers, the XML Schema unsignedShort type.
  • Flags: a single character, and the case is not significant.
  • Service: a character string of unspecified maximum length, with values that depend on the application.
  • Regular Expression: a character string of unspecified maximum length. It can contain many backslashes and should be treated with care.
  • Replacement: a domain name, as a character string of at most 255 characters.
sections.eli5: Each phone number entry is a list of cards. Each card says what kind of contact it is, in what order to try it, and where to send the call or message.

sections.title: Extension Elements in EPP Commands
sections.content:
The extension lives in the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:e164epp-1.0 and goes inside the EPP <extension> element. Each NAPTR is an <e164:naptr> element with <e164:order>, <e164:pref>, an optional <e164:flags>, <e164:svc>, an optional <e164:regex> and an optional <e164:replacement>.

Only some commands change:

  • info: the command is unchanged, but the response <extension> MUST contain an <e164:infData> element with one or more NAPTR elements.
  • create: the command MUST contain an <extension> with an <e164:create> element holding one or more NAPTR elements. The create response is unchanged.
  • update: the command MUST contain an <e164:update> element with one or more <e164:add> or <e164:rem> elements, each holding a NAPTR. The update response is unchanged.
  • check, transfer, delete and renew: nothing is added.

An EPP error response MUST be returned if an extended info command cannot be processed for any reason.
sections.eli5: Most registry actions stay the same. Only creating an entry, changing an entry and looking one up get extra boxes for the contact cards.

sections.title: Example Commands
sections.content:
The examples use the domain name 3.8.0.0.6.9.2.3.6.1.4.4.e164.arpa. A create command adds two NAPTR records, both with order 10 and flag u: preference 100 with service E2U+sip and regular expression "!^.*$!sip:info@example.com!", and preference 102 with service E2U+msg and "!^.*$!mailto:info@example.com!". The info response returns the same two records inside <e164:infData>, alongside the normal domain data.

The update example removes the E2U+msg record with an <e164:rem> element. When an extended create or update succeeds, the EPP response is as described in the domain mapping.
sections.eli5: In the example, a number gets two contact cards: one for an internet phone call and one for email. Later the email card is taken away.

sections.title: The Formal Schema
sections.content:
The XML Schema in the RFC is the formal definition, suitable for automated validation. It declares create and update as child elements of commands and a global naptr element. A naptrType is a sequence of order and pref (both unsignedShort), optional flags, required svc, optional regex and an optional replacement element.

Flags are a one-character token matching a letter or digit. The service and regex tokens need at least one character. The replacement token has a length from 1 to 255. The create, add, rem and infData types each hold one or more NAPTR elements.
sections.eli5: The schema is the rulebook that a computer uses to check that a form was filled in correctly.

sections.title: Security and Internationalization
sections.content:
The extension provides no security services beyond those of EPP, the domain name mapping and the protocol layers EPP runs over. The security considerations of ENUM and of DDDS and NAPTR (RFC 3403) apply as well.

As with other domain object transforms, transform operations MUST be restricted to the sponsoring client, authenticated by the mechanisms in sections 2.9.1.1 and 7 of RFC 3730. Any attempt by another client MUST be rejected with an appropriate EPP authorization error.

For internationalization, EPP is XML, which natively supports Unicode, and UTF-8 is RECOMMENDED where parsers disagree on encodings. The elements and values here MUST inherit the internationalization conventions of the domain mapping.
sections.eli5: Only the registrar who looks after a number may change its entry. Anyone else gets a polite but firm no.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: Following the XML registry mechanism in RFC 3688, IANA completed two registrations, both with the IESG as registrant contact. One is the namespace URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:e164epp-1.0. The other is the schema URI urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:e164epp-1.0, whose XML is the Formal Syntax section of the RFC.
sections.eli5: The two names used for this extension were written down in an official list so nobody else uses them.
